items.title: 뎀나가 구찌의 엔진에 시동을 걸었다
items.summary: Vogue Korea's review of Demna's second Gucci show (SS2027, Milan, Sept 25) staged inside a mock Gucci store at Allianz Mi-Co, previewing the brand's new retail concept ahead of an October Paris flagship. Coverage is largely positive, framing the collection as a stabilizing, commercially legible step after a turbulent creative transition, with Demna prioritizing 'lightness and speed' and a more wearable, less conceptual direction than his SS26 debut.

items.title: ミラノ・コレクション2026-27年秋冬 デムナの「グッチ」ほか新任デザイナーが相次ぐ
items.summary: WWD Japan's Milan Fashion Week feature situates Demna's second Gucci show among a wave of new-designer debuts (Fendi, Marni) this season, noting the show drew over 1.7 million SNS mentions around air time -- described as the single largest buzz spike of the week. Framing is measured trade coverage rather than pure celebration, treating Gucci as one contender in a crowded 'new creative director' cycle rather than a clear winner.

items.title: ミラノファッションウィーク26-27年秋冬──賛否巻き起こしたデムナのグッチ、フェンディとマルニも新章
items.summary: Japanese fashion trade outlet explicitly frames Demna's Gucci show as having sparked '賛否' (mixed praise and criticism) rather than unanimous acclaim, grouping it with Fendi's and Marni's own new-chapter debuts this Milan season. Piece treats the divided reaction itself as the headline, a more balanced framing than typical activation coverage.

items.source: Sina Fashion Hourly Digest (新浪时尚热点小时报)
items.title: 新浪时尚热点小时报丨2026年09月25日19时
items.summary: Weibo-linked hourly entertainment/fashion digest reports Chinese actor Song Weilong's appearance at the Gucci Milan show generated a trending hashtag (#宋威龙), described in fan-style language as looking like he 'stepped out of a Gucci menswear editorial.' Coverage is celebrity-fashion-moment framing typical of Chinese fan/SNS amplification around Milan Fashion Week rather than commentary on the collection itself; illustrates how Gucci buzz in China is substantially driven by attending celebrities rather than the clothes.

items.title: Gucci打破传统推'中国制造'运动鞋 业内人士：恐削弱品牌形象
items.summary: Hong Kong outlet follow-up on Gucci's 'Drip' sneaker, made in China and priced around EUR800/USD1,000, breaking the brand's Italian-manufacturing convention. Cites unnamed industry sources warning the origin label could undercut the luxury repositioning Gucci is trying to build under Demna, and notes Gucci's own statement that Italy remains 'core' to its identity while it partners with Chinese manufacturers for technical reasons, comparable to Swiss/Japanese supplier deals for watches and eyewear. Critical-angle item balancing the show's positive coverage.

items.title: 古驰大降价+新总监首秀，能重现辉煌吗？3个维度深度解读
items.summary: Weibo long-form explainer post links Gucci's September China price cuts (up to 40% on select bags) with Demna's creative reset, asking readers across three angles (pricing logic, design direction, market timing) whether the combination can restore Gucci's standing. Skeptical-leaning framing treats the price cuts as an admission that Gucci overreached on pricing rather than a confident strategic move, echoing broader Chinese consumer distrust of 'discount now, regret later' luxury pricing. Critical/community-sentiment angle rather than brand-marketing amplification.
